questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why animals make better pets than robots
How new medicines are sold around the world
The history of animal rights campaigns in Britain and Europe
How artificial intelligence could reduce testing on animals
questions.why: Georgie says they'll hear how AI could help reduce the need for testing on animals.

questions.q: Why do animal rights campaigners oppose animal testing?
options: They say it is too expensive for companies
They say it is cruel and doesn't work well
They say it takes too long
They say it is illegal in most countries
questions.why: Campaigners say it's cruel, and also ineffective because animals and humans are so different.

questions.q: What does British law say about testing medicines?
options: Medicines can only be tested on healthy human volunteers
Animal testing has been banned
They must be tested on two different types of animals
Only AI can be used to test them
questions.why: Phil says medicines must be tested on two different types of animals.

questions.q: What problem with animal testing does Christine Ro describe?
options: Results in animals don't always match what happens in humans
Animals are too small to test medicines on
Scientists often lose the test results
Mice and dogs always react in exactly the same way as people
questions.why: She says substances toxic in animals have been safe in humans, and vice versa.

questions.q: What does Christine think most people would want?
options: Testing to continue in exactly the same way as now
Medicines tested only on pets
As few animals used as possible, while staying safe
No new medicines to be made
questions.why: She says most people would want as few animals, or none, used while still ensuring safety.

questions.q: Why is AI useful for checking chemical safety?
options: It can analyse enormous amounts of data
It can grow human cells in a lab
It replaces the need for any scientists
It makes medicines cheaper to produce
questions.why: Georgie says one thing AI is really good at is analysing mountains of data.

questions.q: Why does Christine mention the number of new chemicals being invented?
options: To show that scientists are working too slowly
To argue that all new chemicals should be banned until tested
To explain why animal testing is getting cheaper
To show that the amount of data to check keeps growing
questions.why: On top of the huge amount of data, there's a staggering number of new chemicals all the time.

questions.q: What warning does Christine give about AI?
options: It is far too dangerous to be used in medicine at all
It is important, but it isn't the complete answer
It will make animal testing more common
It only works for simple medicines
questions.why: She says “AI isn't the whole picture” but it's an increasingly important part.
